target: Até onde eu sei, o projeto foi aprovado.
english: As far as I know, the project was approved.
tip: 'Até onde eu sei' + indicative – states speaker's knowledge.

target: Uma vez que a decisão foi tomada, não há como voltar atrás.
english: Once the decision has been made, there's no going back.
tip: 'Uma vez que' means 'since/given that'.

target: Desde que eu me lembro, ele sempre foi assim.
english: As far as I can remember, he's always been like that.
tip: 'Desde que' can mean 'since' (time) or 'as long as' (condition).

target: Estou trabalhando de casa hoje.
english: I'm working from home today.
tip: Estar + gerúndio (-ando, -endo, -indo) forms the present continuous in Brazilian Portuguese.

target: À medida que envelhecemos, ficamos mais sábios.
english: As we age, we become wiser.
tip: 'À medida que' means 'as/to the extent that' – indicates parallel progression.

target: Ele tornou a ligar no dia seguinte.
english: He called again the next day.
tip: 'Tornar a' + infinitive = to do something again – formal.

target: Ou seja, a reunião foi cancelada.
english: In other words, the meeting was canceled.
tip: 'Ou seja' = 'in other words/that is'.

target: Tenho de admitir que você tinha razão.
english: I have to admit you were right.
tip: 'Ter de' + infinitive is slightly more formal than 'ter que'.

target: A despeito das críticas, o projeto seguiu em frente.
english: Despite the criticism, the project moved forward.
tip: 'A despeito de' is a formal synonym of 'apesar de'.

target: Ela costuma acordar cedo durante a semana.
english: She usually wakes up early during the week.
tip: 'Costumar' + infinitive = to usually do something – habitual action.

target: Em face dos acontecimentos, decidimos cancelar.
english: In light of the events, we decided to cancel.
tip: 'Em face de' = 'in light of/in the face of'.

target: Conforme combinamos, a reunião será às dez.
english: As we agreed, the meeting will be at ten.
tip: 'Conforme' = 'as/according to'.

target: Porquanto os dados são confiáveis, podemos avançar.
english: Since the data is reliable, we can proceed.
tip: 'Porquanto' is very formal – 'inasmuch as/since'.

target: Bem como seus colegas, ela recebeu o certificado.
english: Like her colleagues, she received the certificate.
tip: 'Bem como' = 'as well as'.

target: Ela mencionou que estava pensando em mudar de cidade.
english: She mentioned she was thinking about moving to another city.
tip: 'pensando' – gerund form for ongoing action. Brazilian Portuguese prefers 'estar + gerund' over European Portuguese's 'estar a + infinitive'.

target: Contanto que você estude, pode sair à noite.
english: As long as you study, you can go out at night.
tip: 'Contanto que' always takes the subjunctive.

target: Ele vive reclamando da vida.
english: He's always complaining about life.
tip: 'Viver' + gerúndio = to always be doing something – habitual.

target: Ele volta e meia esquece as chaves.
english: He keeps forgetting his keys.
tip: 'Volta e meia' = every now and then/keeps on.

target: Não sei se ele está mentindo.
english: I don't know if he's lying.
tip: 'mentindo' – gerund form for ongoing action. Brazilian Portuguese prefers 'estar + gerund' over European Portuguese's 'estar a + infinitive'.

target: Eles continuam morando no mesmo bairro.
english: They continue living in the same neighborhood.
tip: 'Continuar' + gerúndio = to continue doing.

target: Você tem que entregar o relatório até sexta.
english: You have to submit the report by Friday.
tip: 'Ter que' + infinitive = to have to. Slightly more informal than 'ter de'.

target: Ele disse que ia ligar no dia seguinte.
english: He said he would call the next day.
tip: 'Amanhã' becomes 'no dia seguinte' in reported speech.

target: Ele perguntou se eu queria ir ao cinema.
english: He asked if I wanted to go to the movies.
tip: Questions in reported speech use 'se' (if/whether) instead of direct question form.

target: Ela me contou que ia viajar no feriado.
english: She told me she was going to travel on the holiday.
tip: 'Contar que' (to tell/recount that) introduces reported narratives – more personal than 'dizer que'.

target: A gente se fala, falou?
english: We'll talk later, deal?
tip: 'Falou' at the end = 'deal?/okay?' – informal confirmation.

target: Ela é muito gata, todo mundo concorda.
english: She's really hot, everyone agrees.
tip: 'Gato/gata' = hot/attractive person – common Brazilian slang.

target: Que ele faça o que quiser.
english: Let him do whatever he wants.
tip: Subjunctive used in the third person to express 'let him/her'.

target: Ela disse que tinha terminado o trabalho.
english: She said she had finished the work.
tip: Past tense shifts to pluperfect: 'terminei' → 'tinha terminado'.

target: Dado que todos concordam, podemos avançar.
english: Given that everyone agrees, we can move forward.
tip: 'Dado que' + indicative when stating a fact.

target: Há que se reconhecer que houve avanços significativos.
english: One must acknowledge that there were significant advances.
tip: 'Há que se' + infinitive = 'one must' – impersonal.

target: Quer queira, quer não, vai ter que ir.
english: Whether he likes it or not, he'll have to go.
tip: 'Quer... quer' + subjunctive = 'whether... or'.

target: Tenho certeza de que ele vem.
english: I'm sure he's coming.
tip: 'Ter certeza de que' takes the indicative – it expresses certainty.

target: Ficou massa essa comida!
english: This food turned out awesome!
tip: 'Massa' = awesome/great – common in Northeastern Brazilian slang.

target: Eu insisto que ele está errado.
english: I insist that he's wrong.
tip: 'Insistir que' + indicative when asserting a belief/fact.

target: Eu talvez vou à festa.
english: I might go to the party.
tip: When 'talvez' comes after the subject, the indicative is sometimes used in casual speech.

target: O supracitado relatório encontra-se em anexo.
english: The aforementioned report is attached herein.
tip: 'Supracitado' is formal bureaucratic language – 'aforementioned'.

target: Se bem que ele tem um ponto.
english: Although, he does have a point.
tip: 'Se bem que' takes indicative – it introduces a concession of fact.

target: Aqui é raiz, não tem frescura!
english: We keep it real here, no faking it!
tip: 'Raiz' = authentic/real. 'Frescura' = pretense/fussiness.

target: Ela é show de bola, faz tudo direitinho.
english: She's awesome, she does everything just right.
tip: 'Show de bola' = awesome/fantastic – informal expression.

target: Se eu tenho tempo, gosto de ler.
english: If I have time, I like to read.
tip: 'Se' + indicative for general truths/habits.

target: Ele é muito pão-duro, nunca paga nada.
english: He's so stingy, he never pays for anything.
tip: 'Pão-duro' = stingy person – common Brazilian expression.

target: Quando a verdade vier à tona, todos saberão.
english: When the truth comes out, everyone will know.
tip: 'vier' – future subjunctive, used after 'quando', 'se', 'enquanto' for events that may happen. Unique to Portuguese among Romance languages.

target: Se eu tiver tempo, passo na sua casa.
english: If I have time, I'll stop by your place.
tip: 'tiver' – future subjunctive, used after 'quando', 'se', 'enquanto' for events that may happen. Unique to Portuguese among Romance languages.

target: Manda a real, você gostou ou não?
english: Tell me straight–did you like it or not?
tip: 'Mandar a real' = to be honest/tell the truth – slang.

target: Estou com a cabeça nas nuvens hoje.
english: I'm daydreaming today.
tip: 'Estar com a cabeça nas nuvens' = to have one's head in the clouds.

target: Partiu praia no fim de semana?
english: Beach trip this weekend?
tip: 'Partiu' + noun = 'let's go to' – very popular informal expression.

target: Ela deu conta do recado.
english: She got the job done.
tip: 'Dar conta do recado' = to accomplish the task.

target: Ela está com a corda toda hoje!
english: She's full of energy today!
tip: 'Estar com a corda toda' = to be full of energy/enthusiastic.

target: Fala sério! Não acredito nisso.
english: Come on! I can't believe that.
tip: 'Fala sério' = come on/no way – disbelief expression.

target: Fica frio, vai dar tudo certo.
english: Chill out, everything will be fine.
tip: 'Fica frio' = stay cool/chill – very informal.

target: Tu é ligeirão, hein? Resolveu tudo rapidinho.
english: You're quick, huh? Solved everything fast.
tip: 'Ligeirão' = fast/quick person – informal.

target: Ele está vendendo o almoço para pagar o jantar.
english: He's robbing Peter to pay Paul.
tip: 'Vender o almoço para pagar o jantar' = to barely make ends meet.

target: Esse carioca é sangue bom demais!
english: This guy from Rio has such good vibes!
tip: 'Sangue bom' = good person/cool – carioca slang.

target: Ela é a menina dos olhos do pai.
english: She's the apple of her father's eye.
tip: 'Menina dos olhos' = apple of one's eye.

target: Cara, essa festa vai ser irada!
english: Dude, this party is going to be awesome!
tip: 'Cara' = dude. 'Irada' = awesome/sick – brazilian slang.

target: Prezado senhor, venho por meio desta solicitar informações.
english: Dear sir, I am writing to request information.
tip: Highly formal letter opening – 'venho por meio desta' is standard business Portuguese.

target: Tá osso conseguir emprego nessa cidade.
english: It's rough to get a job in this city.
tip: 'Tá osso' = it's hard/difficult – informal expression.

target: Não vou dar mole, vou estudar muito.
english: I'm not going to slack off, I'll study hard.
tip: 'Dar mole' = to slack off/let one's guard down.

target: Pô, que vacilo! Esqueci a carteira em casa.
english: Man, what a blunder! I forgot my wallet at home.
tip: 'Pô' = man/dude (exclamation). 'Vacilo' = mistake/blunder.

target: Não fosse a ajuda dos vizinhos, teríamos perdido tudo.
english: Were it not for the neighbors' help, we would have lost everything.
tip: 'Não fosse' = 'were it not for' – inverted conditional without 'se'.
